Senses.Note: To distinguish black from white is to discriminate clearly between what an encounter, saying, or lineage claim does and does not amount to. Masters demand this hair's-breadth discrimination and condemn indiscriminate handling.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB406.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baoning: Baoning Renyong bears the exact headword. Baoning says one must distinguish black from white, since a hair's breadth weighs more than mountains.
Source record (T/T47/T47n1997.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu: Yuanwu Keqin bears the exact headword. Yuanwu says the Four Classifications distinguish black from white.
Source record (J/J26/J26nB178.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan: Poshan Haiming bears the exact headword. Poshan condemns following others without distinguishing black from white.
Source record (J/J27/J27nB194.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Muchen: Muchen Daomin bears the exact headword. Muchen calls for someone able to distinguish black from white and know the weight.
Source record (J/J29/J29nB233.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Feiyin: Feiyin Tongrong bears the exact headword. Feiyin condemns people who do not know black from white yet speak recklessly.
